text: EX-99.1 2 exhibit991-9302026.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE FOR MORE INFORMATION CONTACT: 11/4/2026 Investors: Dexter Congbalay, investor.relations@us.mcd.com Media: Lauren Altmin, lauren.altmin@us.mcd.com McDONALD'S REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS • Global Systemwide sales* increased 4% to over $38 billion for the quarter • Consolidated operating income increased 7% and adjusted operating income increased 8% for the quarter • Systemwide sales to loyalty members across 70 loyalty markets were $41 billion for the trailing twelve-month period and more than $11 billion for the quarter CHICAGO, IL - McDonald's Corporation today announced results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. “McDonald’s delivered another quarter of global growth, with solid performance across much of our international business. In the U.S., we're encouraged by improvement as the quarter progressed following our intervention on value,” said Chris Kempczinski, Chairman and CEO. “We’re focused on building from here, strengthening the business today and investing in the next chapter of growth.” Third quarter financial performance: • Global comparable sales increased 1.5%: • U.S. decreased 0.2% • International Operated Markets increased 1.4% • International Developmental Licensed Markets increased 4.2% • Consolidated revenues increased 1% (1% in constant currencies). • Systemwide sales increased 4% (4% in constant currencies). • Consolidated operating income increased 7% (7% in constant currencies). Results reflected pre-tax charges of $56 million and $39 million for the current year and prior year, respectively, primarily related to restructuring charges associated with Accelerating the Organization. Excluding these current and prior year charges, consolidated operating income increased 8% (8% in constant currencies).** • Diluted earnings per share was $3.51, an increase of 10% (11% in constant currencies). Excluding the current year charges described above of $0.06 per share, diluted earnings per share was $3.57, an increase of 11% (11% in constant currencies) when also excluding prior year charges.** • The Company declared a 4% increase in its quarterly cash dividend to $1.93 per share. *Refer to page 4 for a definition of Systemwide sales. **Refer to pages 2 and 3 for additional details on our results for the third quarter 2026 and 2025. 1 COMPARABLE SALES Increase/(Decrease) Quarters Ended September 30, 2026 2025 U.S. (0.2) % 2.4 % International Operated Markets 1.4 4.3 International Developmental Licensed Markets 4.2 4.7 Total Company 1.5 % 3.6 % • U.S.: Comparable sales declined slightly as negative comparable guest counts were largely offset by positive check growth. • International Operated Markets: Most markets reflected positive comparable sales, led by Germany and Australia, partly offset by France. • International Developmental Licensed Markets: All geographic regions reflected positive comparable sales. Positive comparable sales were led by Japan, partly offset by negative comparable sales in China. Management reviews and analyzes business results excluding the effect of foreign currency translation, impairment and other charges and gains, as well as material regulatory and other income tax impacts, and bases incentive compensation plans on these results because the Company believes this better represents underlying business trends. Comparable sales and comparable guest counts are compared to the same period in the prior year and represent sales and transactions, respectively, at all restaurants, whether owned and operated by the Company or by franchisees, in operation at least thirteen months, including those temporarily closed. Some of the reasons restaurants may be temporarily closed include reimaging or remodeling, rebuilding, road construction, natural disasters, pandemics and acts of war, terrorism or other hostilities. Comparable sales exclude the impact of currency translation and the sales of any market considered hyperinflationary (generally identified as those markets whose cumulative inflation rate over a three-year period exceeds 100%), which management believes more accurately reflects the underlying business trends. Comparable sales are driven by changes in guest counts and average check, the latter of which is affected by changes in pricing and product mix. Systemwide sales include sales at all restaurants, whether owned and operated by the Company or by franchisees. Systemwide sales to loyalty members are comprised of all sales to customers who self-identify as a loyalty member when transacting with both Company-owned and operated and franchised restaurants. Systemwide sales to loyalty members are measured across 70 markets with loyalty programs. Systemwide sales to loyalty members represents an aggregation of the prior four quarters of sales to loyalty members active in the last 90 days of the respective quarter. While franchised sales are not recorded as revenues by the Company, management believes the information is important in understanding the Company's financial performance because these sales are the basis on which the Company calculates and records franchised revenues and are indicative of the financial health of the franchisee base. The Company's revenues consist of sales by Company-owned and operated restaurants and fees from franchised restaurants operated by conventional franchisees, developmental licensees and affiliates. Changes in Systemwide sales are primarily driven by comparable sales and net restaurant unit expansion. Free cash flow , defined as cash provided by operations less capital expenditures, and free cash flow conversion rate, defined as free cash flow divided by net income, are measures reviewed by management in order to evaluate the Company’s ability to convert net profits into cash resources, after reinvesting in the core business, that can be used to pursue opportunities to enhance shareholder value. ABOUT McDONALD’S McDonald’s is the world’s leading global foodservice retailer with over 45,000 locations in over 100 countries. Approximately 95% of McDonald’s restaurants worldwide are owned and operated by independent local business owners.
